summary: The note is a cybersecurity checklist for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), prompted by stepped-up industry efforts since September 2023 to serve businesses with limited resources and expertise. It covers risk assessment, employee training, patching, passwords and 2FA, backups, email security, network protection, audits, mobile security, vendor risk, insurance, investment, and security culture. Quotes from business owners and experts illustrate each point.
one_line: A checklist of cybersecurity practices for SMEs, from risk assessment and training to backups, insurance and building a security culture, with expert quotes.
key_facts: Since the beginning of September 2023, cybersecurity firms and tech innovators have stepped up efforts to support SMEs in protecting digital assets.
John Kendrick, CEO of Tech Solutions, adopted a more vigilant stance after a close call with a phishing scam in late 2023.
Customer data, intellectual property, and financial information typically top the list of assets needing the most robust defenses.
Maria Alvarez, a cybersecurity education advocate, developed tailored training for small businesses so cybersecurity knowledge is part of every employee's skill set.
Small businesses are advised to turn on automatic updates and routinely check for patches that must be applied manually.
Christopher Yu, IT manager for a growing eCommerce platform, says disciplined patch management saved the business from numerous attacks exploiting outdated systems.
Password policies should require regular password changes, and two-factor authentication (2FA) should be the norm.
Sarah O'Neil, owner of a boutique marketing firm, was hit by ransomware in October 2023 but restored critical data with minimal downtime thanks to her backup routine.
Nathanial Green, CTO of Midtown Analytics, says advanced email security reduced the company's phishing incidents by 80%.
Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS) and advanced cybersecurity AI are now within the financial reach of many SMEs.
Mobile devices used for remote work should be covered by security policies, including the use of Virtual Private Networks (VPNs).
Sam Patel, a cybersecurity consultant for retail SMEs, says vendor risk management is necessary to extend cybersecurity posture beyond the business's own boundaries.
Cybersecurity insurance can cover data recovery costs, legal liabilities, and reputation management.
The note says a security-focused culture should be driven by top management and permeate all levels of the organization.
